answer.rationale: Three pressures compete for the single experiment slot, but the primary objective is sustainable long-term qualified revenue, not short-term acquisition. Promotional pricing (memory_73) is the most tempting response to competitor pricing pressure, but its own record flags a pooled-cohort redefinition mid-test, meaning the acquisition/revenue lift figure is not cleanly attributable and could mask attraction of low-quality, price-sensitive, high-churn accounts—exactly the segment a competitor is currently price-cutting to acquire. Racing to match pricing without resolving that caveat risks trading long-term qualified revenue for short-term signups. Onboarding simplification (memory_31) has a cleaner, durable, previously-consolidated result, and it directly addresses two of the three concurrent problems (activation down 6%, onboarding completion down 4%) with lower downstream risk to revenue quality. I verify memory_73 to check whether the pooled-cohort issue can be resolved or whether it should be excluded from consideration this cycle, and memory_31 to confirm the onboarding lift record still holds up before committing the week's only experiment slot to it. Pending that check, my intended action is to run the onboarding simplification experiment at standard scale, not a broad rollout, since activation/onboarding declines warrant a real test but not yet full commitment, and to hold promotional pricing in reserve until its evidence base is clarified rather than reacting reflexively to competitive pressure.
